text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Archbishop voices concern over divorce, saying it would bring disorder in family and society; government announces commission on divorce; Malta is only European country not to have divorce.

- Prime minister hints at possibility of compromise on postal service; government winding down state-owned company responsible for service and has said it intends making Posts Department part of civil service again.
- Former government agreed with European Bank for all households to pay annual fee for sewage connections, prime minister says.

- Prime minister condemns Broadcasting Authority for upholding opposition protests over government advertisements on new tax system; authority agreed with Nationalist Party that advertising included politically controversial material.

- Hysterical attack against Broadcasting Authority. Nationalist Party attacks prime minister after he criticises Authority; party says prime minister, as minister responsible for broadcasting, should have ensured that public broadcasting was fair.
